from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Tiny block collides with a massive block.",
            "The number of bounces is surprisingly huge.",
            "Mass ratios unlock the digits of Pi."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: A Paradoxical Counting Puzzle", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create physical components
        wall = Line(UP, DOWN, color=GREY).scale(1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(wall, "C1")
        
        tiny = Square(side_length=0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8)
        huge = Square(side_length=0.8, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8)
        
        self.place_at_grid(tiny, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(huge, "C5")
        
        # Velocity vectors
        v_tiny = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*0.5, color=WHITE)
        v_huge = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=LEFT*0.3, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(wall), FadeIn(tiny), FadeIn(huge))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(v_tiny), Create(v_huge))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        # Animate movement
        self.play(
            tiny.animate.next_to(huge, LEFT, buff=0.1),
            v_tiny.animate.next_to(tiny, UP, buff=0.1),
            v_huge.animate.next_to(huge, UP, buff=0.1),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        # Flash vectors
        self.play(
            v_tiny.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            v_huge.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            v_tiny.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            v_huge.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=0.5
        )

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Geometry of Collisions: The Phase Space Arc", 
                          ["Energy forms an ellipse in phase space.", 
                           "Collisions are boundary reflections in a slice.", 
                           "Trajectory arcs define the bounce count."])
        
        # Create visual elements
        # Axes for phase space
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A2", "F5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Ellipse representing energy conservation
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=3, height=1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(ellipse, "A2", "F5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Boundary lines for collisions (slice)
        line1 = Line(start=np.array([-1, -1, 0]), end=np.array([1, 1, 0]), color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(line1, "A2", "F5", scale_factor=1)
        
        # Trajectory arc
        arc = Arc(radius=1.5, start_angle=PI/4, angle=PI/2, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(arc, "A2", "F5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(ellipse))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(Create(line1))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(Create(arc))
        
        # Finalize
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Reveal: Linking Physics to Pi", [
            "Mass ratio shrinks the pie-slice angle.",
            "The trajectory unrolls along a circular arc.",
            "It physically computes digits of Pi."
        ])

        # Assets
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        self.place_in_area(circle, "A2", "D5")

        self.place_in_area(arc, "A2", "D5")
        
        pi_text = MathTex(r"\pi \approx 3.14159", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_text, "E3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Mass ratio shrinks the pie-slice angle.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        wedge = Sector(radius=1.5, angle=0.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(wedge, "A2", "D5")
        self.add(wedge)
        self.play(Create(wedge), run_time=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The trajectory unrolls along a circular arc.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(Create(arc), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # It physically computes digits of Pi.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Indicate(pi_text), run_time=2)
        
        # Final highlight
        self.play(pi_text.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), run_time=1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", [
            "Discretized physics meets continuous geometry.", 
            "Complex dynamics reveal hidden mathematical constants.", 
            "Simple collisions map to deep numbers."
        ])
        
        # Define mobjects
        collision_visual = VGroup(
            Square(color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.5),
            Square(color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.8)
        ).arrange(RIGHT)
        
        pi_text = MathTex(r"\pi \approx 3.14159...").scale(1.2)
        
        chain = VGroup(collision_visual, Arrow(), pi_text).arrange(DOWN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_in_area(chain, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.play(
            FadeOut(collision_visual),
            pi_text.animate.set_color("#FF00FF").scale(1.2).move_to(self.grid["C3"])
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(pi_text, color="#FFFF00", buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Pi-Collision Paradox: Why Bouncing Blocks Count Digits of Pi
outline.target_audience: University students (Physics/Math) or curious high schoolers

sections.title: The Hook: A Paradoxical Counting Puzzle
sections.content: Introduce a 1D physics scenario: A small block of mass m and a large block of mass M (where M = 100^n * m) collide on a frictionless surface against a wall. The question: How many total collisions occur before the blocks stop moving toward the wall?
sections.example: Visualize two blocks, 'Tiny' and 'Huge', on a track. As the mass ratio increases (1:1, 1:100, 1:10000), the number of collisions grows surprisingly to 3, 31, 314...

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Elastic Collision & Conservation
sections.content: Briefly explain the Conservation of Momentum and Kinetic Energy. Use a vector diagram to show how velocity changes sign during a collision between two masses, setting the stage for the 'state space' representation.
sections.example: A rubber ball bouncing off a bowling ball. We represent the velocities of both blocks as coordinates (v1, v2) on a 2D plane.

sections.title: The Geometry of Collisions: The Phase Space Arc
sections.content: Introduce the 'Phase Space' concept. Show that conservation of energy forms an ellipse in this space. Collisions are represented as lines crossing the axes. The number of collisions equals the number of times the state trajectory crosses the 'boundary' lines.
sections.example: An animation showing a point bouncing off two 'walls' in a pie-slice-shaped region of the phase space, tracing a circular arc.

sections.title: The Reveal: Linking Physics to Pi
sections.content: Explain that as the mass ratio M/m grows, the angle of the pie-slice becomes smaller (specifically arcsin(sqrt(m/M))). The trajectory effectively 'unrolls' the circle. The number of hits corresponds to the digits of Pi.
sections.example: Overlay the trajectory arc onto a circle diagram. Show that for M = 1,000,000 * m, the result is exactly 3141 collisions—the first four digits of Pi.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap the deep connection: Discretized physics (collisions) converges to continuous geometry (Pi). Emphasize how complex dynamic systems often hide fundamental mathematical constants.
sections.example: A final visual showing the blocks colliding, then transitioning into the digits of Pi (3.14159...) appearing one by one as the collision counter increments.
